## Set up local tempfolder for raw and processed data files
```{r local-tempfolder}
# Get the path to the session's temporary directory
session_temp_dir <- tempdir()

# Define paths for the specific temporary subdirectories
raw_data_dir <- file.path(session_temp_dir, "raw_data")
processed_data_dir <- file.path(session_temp_dir, "processed_data")

# Create the 'raw_data' subdirectory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(raw_data_dir)) {
  dir.create(raw_data_dir)
}

# Create the 'processed_data' subdirectory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(processed_data_dir)) {
  dir.create(processed_data_dir)
}

 
```

# Download Zotero_SynthesisTable.csv 
```{r get-processed-data-osf, echo=TRUE, include=TRUE, results='hide'}

osf_retrieve_node(processed_data_node_id) %>%
  osf_ls_files(pattern = "Zotero_SynthesisTable.csv") %>%
   osf_download(path = raw_data_dir, conflicts="overwrite",progress=TRUE)

```

## Load Zotero tag export file into R data frame
```{r list-csv-files}

csv_file <- list.files(path = raw_data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

if (length(csv_file) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No csv file found in the specified directory.")
}



# standard pathname
csv_file[1] <- file.path(dirname(csv_file[1]), basename(csv_file[1]))
if (!file.exists(csv_file[1])) {
  stop("File does not exist. Check the path.")
}

print(csv_file)
```

# Select first CSV file

```{r load-csv-file}
# Read the file
Zotero_SynthesisTable <- read.csv(csv_file[1], encoding = "UTF-8")

# Check if the file is empty
if (length(Zotero_SynthesisTable) == 0) {
  stop("Error: The csv file is empty.")
}

```

########## manupulations 

```{r rename dataset}
# Rename the dataframe
datacleaningtable <- Zotero_SynthesisTable
```

```{r remove dotes headers}
# Remove all dots from column names
colnames(datacleaningtable) <- gsub("\\.", "", colnames(datacleaningtable))
```


```{r alfabtic order columns}
# new order
datacleaningtable <- datacleaningtable[, order(colnames(datacleaningtable))]

```

```{r merge to new}

# Define column groups for merging
columns_methods <- c("method_qualitative","method_quantitative", "method_mixed", "method_qualitative_interpreted")

columns_disciplines <- c("discipline_accountant", "discipline_arts","discipline_economics", "discipline_entrepreneurship", "discipline_ethics", "discipline_interdisciplinairy", "discipline_innovation", "discipline_leadership", "discipline_management", "discipline_marketing", "discipline_sustainability", "discipline_strategy", "discipline_changemanagement", "discipline_supplychain", "discipline_HR", "discipline_organisational")

columns_context <- c("business_context", "higher_education")

columns_objectives <- c("aim", "research_question", "hypothesis")

columns_locations <- c("location_europe", "location_nordamerica", "location_asia", "location_southamerica", "location_online", "location_australia", "location_europe_secundary", "location_nordamerica_secundary", "location_southamerica_secundary", "location_africa")

columns_intergration <- c("artsrelated", "artsbased", "artsinformed", "intergration_unclear")

columns_results <- c("result_teaching", "result_proces", "result_motivation", 
                     "result_outcome", "result_perspective", 
                     "result_organisational_outcome")

columns_arts_forms <- c("art_making", "artform", "form_diverse", 
                     "form_multimedia", "form_narrative", "form_theatre", 
                     "form_visual")

columns_arts_reasons <- c("reason_art", "reason_artmaking", "reason_multimedia", "reason_music", 
                     "reason_narrative", "reason_theatre", "reason_theatre", 
                     "reason_visual")


# Function to merge selected columns into one while keeping column names
merge_columns <- function(df, new_column, old_columns) {
  df %>%
    mutate(!!new_column := apply(.[old_columns], 1, function(x) {
      paste(names(x)[!is.na(x) & x != ""], x[!is.na(x) & x != ""], sep = ": ", collapse = "; ")
    })) %>%
    select(-all_of(old_columns))  # Remove old columns
}

# Apply merging function to each group
datacleaningtable <- datacleaningtable %>%
  merge_columns("methods", columns_methods) %>%
  merge_columns("disciplines", columns_disciplines) %>%
  merge_columns("context", columns_context) %>%
  merge_columns("objectives", columns_objectives) %>%
  merge_columns("locations", columns_locations) %>%
  merge_columns("intergration", columns_intergration) %>%
  merge_columns("results", columns_results) %>%
  merge_columns("arts_forms", columns_arts_forms) %>%
  merge_columns("arts_reasons", columns_arts_reasons) %>%

# Display only the all newly created columns
print(datacleaningtable %>% select(methods, disciplines, context, 
                                   objectives, locations, intergration, results, arts_forms,   arts_reasons), width = Inf)
```


```{r reorder}
# Reorder columns: title first, then the merged ones, then everything else
new_cols <- c("methods", "disciplines", "context", 
              "objectives", "locations", "intergration", "results", "arts_forms", "arts_reasons")

datacleaningtable <- datacleaningtable %>%
  select(title, author, all_of(new_cols), everything())

```

```{r make excel sheet with coloured empty cells}

library(openxlsx)

# Define output path
file_path <- "/Users/Accounttijdelijk/Desktop/datacompletion15.9.2025.xlsx"

# Create a new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# Add a worksheet
addWorksheet(wb, "Data")

# Write the dataframe
writeData(wb, "Data", datacleaningtable)

# Define a red style for empty cells
red_style <- createStyle(fontColour = "#9C0006", bgFill = "#FFC7CE") 

# Find empty cells (either "" or NA)
empty_cells <- which(datacleaningtable == "" | is.na(datacleaningtable), arr.ind = TRUE)

# Apply the style to each empty cell
for (i in seq_len(nrow(empty_cells))) {
  row <- empty_cells[i, 1] + 1   # +1 because of header row
  col <- empty_cells[i, 2]
  addStyle(wb, sheet = "Data", style = red_style, rows = row, cols = col, gridExpand = TRUE)
}

# Save the Excel file
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

cat("Excel file saved to:", normalizePath(file_path), "\n")

```
